# 1 Enoch Chapter 81 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 81 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 81:2 — 'heavenly tablets' — the celestial record

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "heavenly-tablets" | Literal Ge'ez; luchot shamayim equivalent |
| LOGOS | "heavenly tablets" | Standard scholarly rendering |
| PNEUMA | "heavenly tablets" | All three agree |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Converged on 'heavenly tablets.' This is the standard designation for this motif in Second Temple literature (cf. 1 En 93:2; 103:2; 106:19; Jubilees 3:10; 4Q213).

**Status:** Converged.

---

## 81:4 — 'Blessed is the man who dies in righteousness'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Blessed-is-the-man who-dies-in-righteousness and-goodness" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "Blessed is the man who dies in righteousness and goodness" | Standard |
| PNEUMA | "Blessed is the one who dies in righteousness and goodness" | 'One' is gender-inclusive |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'man' (LOGOS/EMET). The Ge'ez uses the masculine 'man' (sab') in a generic but grammatically masculine sense; 'one' (PNEUMA) is inclusive but imposes a modern sensitivity on an ancient text. Project convention favors staying closer to the source.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---

## 81:5 — 'no flesh is righteous in the sight of the Lord'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "no-flesh-is-righteous-in-the-sight-of-the-Lord" | Literal; theological statement |
| LOGOS | "no flesh is righteous in the sight of the Lord" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "no human being is righteous before the Lord" | 'Human being' for 'flesh'; 'before' for 'in the sight of' |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering. 'No flesh is righteous' is the more precise and theologically resonant phrase — 'flesh' (Ge'ez: sega; cf. Hebrew: basar) has specific theological weight in Second Temple literature, denoting human creatureliness and moral limitation. Replacing it with 'human being' (PNEUMA) loses this nuance. The phrase anticipates Romans 3:20 ('no flesh will be justified').

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET. Theological precision preserved.

---
